comments.body:
Census complete against a fresh `origin/main` worktree at `71a719aef88`. Counts reproduced exactly: **51 total failures, 4 SemLock (excluded, `0eba`), 47 in scope.** No nondeterminism — the population is stable.

## Verdict on the ticket's final criterion

**`make verify` can be made green under the sandbox. There is no irreducible residue.** All 47, plus the 4 SemLock failures, are addressable while preserving full CI coverage, using direct capability probes and loud counted local signals.

## Distinct root causes: 5

| Cause | Count |
|---|---:|
| Injected Git command-line identity overrides test-local identity | 20 |
| Wrong-architecture / missing pandoc host binary | 17 |
| Sandboxed home breaks semgrep fallback | 8 |
| Sandbox denies `ps` | 1 |
| Baseline close-gate branch/ref mismatch | 1 |

Every attribution is **probe-confirmed**. None were inferred from traceback alone.

## The reframing: only one of five is actually a sandbox denial

This is the finding that matters most, and it contradicts the ticket's own framing — which I wrote, assuming these were sandbox capability denials like the SemLock four.

- **`ps` (1)** is the only genuine sandbox syscall denial. `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,time=,command=` raises `PermissionError errno=1`.

- **Git identity (20)** is a **harness artifact, not a sandbox restriction**. The harness injects `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=8` with command-line `user.name=Joe Oakhart` / `user.email=joeoakhart@navapbc.com`. Command-line config outranks both repo-local config and a fake `HOME`, so identity-sensitive tests cannot isolate themselves — and tests asserting that a *missing* email aborts instead find one. Removing those `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables makes **28 targeted identity tests pass**. This is the largest single cause and the cheapest to fix.

- **pandoc (17)** is not a sandbox issue at all. The bundled `pypandoc` binary is **`Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64` on an `arm64` host**; executing it raises `OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable`, and no system pandoc is on `PATH`. **This would break for any Apple Silicon developer**, sandboxed or not. It is a dependency packaging defect that the sandbox merely exposed. One test compounds it by then trying `""` and getting `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: ''`.

- **semgrep (8)** is a test-harness environment assumption. `opengrep` is absent; the `semgrep` fallback exists but fails opening the real-home `/Users/joeoakhart/.semgrep/settings.yml` under sandbox EPERM, so detectors abstain and advisory notes read `fail-open-abstain` rather than `detector-finding`. Redirecting `HOME` into worktree scratch makes all 8 pass. Note the deeper issue: availability is tested by `shutil.which`, which reports a binary that cannot actually run.

- **Close-gate (1)** is an **ordinary baseline bug with no environmental component** — see below.

## A real defect found incidentally

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py::test_file_impact_close_fetches_before_rejecting_stale_clone` fails for reasons unrelated to the sandbox. The copied fixture repo is on `master` while the remote commit is on `origin/main`, and `commit_impact.upstream_branch_refs()` only includes refs ending in `/<current-branch>` — so the include-upstream scan ignores `origin/main` even after a successful fetch.

That is a genuine bug in the completion gate's stale-clone handling, not a test artifact, and it is being filed separately. It is adjacent to `8806`, which also concerns the completion gate verifying against the wrong tree.

## Remediation per cause

- **Git identity:** scrub inherited `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` command-line overrides in identity-sensitive tests, or resolve identity through a properly isolated environment. Largest win, smallest change.
- **pandoc:** provide an architecture-correct dependency, or probe by **direct execution** rather than `shutil.which`, with loud counted local unavailability and unchanged CI execution. The packaging defect should be fixed regardless, since it affects arm64 developers generally.
- **semgrep:** run semgrep/opengrep out-of-process with sandboxed `HOME` and tool state, and redefine availability as "can execute a trivial scan" rather than "binary is on `PATH`".
- **`ps`:** the only case needing the probe-and-loud-signal treatment. Preserve CI coverage; emit a counted local signal when a direct `ps` probe fails.
- **Close-gate:** fix as an ordinary bug on its own ticket.

All three hard constraints are satisfiable: CI coverage unchanged, no silent skips, and every detection above is a direct capability probe rather than an environment-name heuristic.

Full traceback log: `.rebar/scratch/1352ecab-4910-4535-9368-1dc8a0029977-20590/make-test.log` in the investigation worktree.

No fixes were implemented, no tracker writes were made, and no push occurred.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
Regression introduced by this ticket's own AC5 change, now blocking the merge pipeline.

`tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_985f.py::test_sandbox_skip_summary_aggregates_across_xdist_workers` fails on GitHub Actions (`ubuntu-latest, py3.11`):

```
>       result.assert_outcomes(skipped=2)
E       AssertionError: assert {'passed': 2,...} == {'passed': 0,...}
tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_985f.py:241: AssertionError
```

Provenance, measured: `git log origin/main -S'test_sandbox_skip_summary_aggregates_across_xdist_workers'` returns exactly one commit, `ddb1d953812` "tests: handle sandbox capability denials" (2026-09-18 04:41 UTC). That is Gerrit change 2980 as rewritten by rebase-on-submit. The test did not exist on `main` before that merge.

Root cause: the assertions encode an ambient-host property rather than the behaviour the test is named for. It asserts `skipped=2` plus stdout `"sandbox ps unavailable: 2"`, which only holds where `ps` is absent - true inside the sandboxed dev environment, false on a CI runner. Where `ps` is present the two inner tests are not skipped, they pass, and the assertion fails. So the test currently discriminates on the host, not on whether cross-worker skip-summary aggregation works.

Blast radius: this is not confined to its own change. It fails for any patchset, so it has already put `Verified -1` on change 2982 (an unrelated autodeploy fix) and change 2983's run is in flight against the same wall. Every change is blocked until it is fixed.

This is not a candidate for `recheck`. The failure is deterministic on a runner with `ps` and deterministic in the other direction here; it is a test defect, not an environmental fault.

Remediation in flight. The bar is a test that passes in both environments and still fails if the aggregation logic it guards is broken - not a `skipif` and not a widened assertion.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Fix for the CI-blocking regression pushed as Gerrit change 2985, commit `be60dc6349a`, single file `tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_985f.py`.

**The diagnosis I dispatched with was partly wrong, and the investigation corrected it.** I reported that the test depended on the ambient host lacking `ps`. That shape is real and reproduces - injecting a fake working `ps` into the inner run makes the inner pytest report `2 passed` and the outer `skipped=2` assertion fail exactly as CI did. But on current `origin/main` the test had already moved off `ps` and was instead depending on **xdist worker placement**, which is scheduler-dependent and equally not the behaviour the test is named for. Same class of defect, different variable. Worth recording because the obvious-looking `ps` story would have produced a fix that left the real nondeterminism in place.

**The fix** forces the capability probe to `CapabilityProbe(False, ...)` inside the inner pytest's conftest and runs the inner session with `-n 2 --dist=each`, so both workers are required to publish counted skips rather than whichever worker happens to receive the tests. The assertions become `skipped=4`, `sandbox compatibility skips: 4`, `sandbox ps unavailable: 4`. The environment is now driven, not inherited.

**Two-environment proof:** the fixed target passes with a fake working `ps` on `PATH`, and passes with `ps` absent from the inner `PATH`. That is the acceptance bar - it no longer discriminates on the host.

**Not-hollowed-out proof:** temporarily disabling `collect_counted_skips_from_worker` makes the target fail, because the counted-skip summary disappears while the 4 inner skips still occur. The test still guards the aggregation behaviour it exists for; it was not widened into vacuity, and it is not a `skipif`.

**Verification:** `make verify` ran to completion and is red only in the documented pre-existing classes - 17 pandoc/wiki-render, 10 doctor, and 5 sandbox/SemLock (`network_guard_local_ipc`, `atomic_completion_close`, `completion_gate`, `marker_fcntl`, `doctor_locks`). `test_sandbox_skip_summary_aggregates_across_xdist_workers` is no longer among them. Focused run of `tests/test_sandbox_capabilities_985f.py` plus `tests/scripts/test_check_orphaned_load.py` gives `46 passed, 1 skipped`; that one skip is a deliberate live-adapter check of the real `ps` parsing path and was correctly left alone.

This change gates three others. 2982, 2983 and 2984 are all sitting on `Verified -1` or awaiting a vote purely because of this test, not for any reason of their own. Once 2985 lands they each need a recheck rather than a rebase.

AC12's count of sandbox failures should be corrected against the post-landing measurement rather than the figure recorded earlier, which predates both this fix and change 2983.

comments.body:
## The 33 are fully partitioned, and only 18 of them are real

Read-only investigation against the surviving `make-test.log` from the `verify-0eba-runs` worktree, with every mechanism confirmed by direct probe rather than inferred from a traceback signature.

| Class | Count | Mechanism | Confirming probe | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Pandoc binary cannot execute | 17 | Rich-text/wiki rendering falls back to raw Markdown because `pypandoc` resolves a bundled pandoc that cannot run; the direct pandoc assertions then execute `""` because `_pandoc_path()` returns falsey | The bundled binary is `Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64`; `--version` on this arm64 host returns `Bad CPU type in executable`, rc 126 | Real, and already ticketed |
| Stale editable install across worktrees | 15 | Tests ran from `verify-0eba-runs`, but the venv's editable install points `rebar` at a different worktree's `src`. Tree-scan tests compute `_REPO_ROOT` from the test checkout and then scan source files resolved from the other checkout, so `Path.relative_to()` raises | `tests._tree_scan` imported from `verify-0eba-runs` while `rebar` imported from `fix-2d65-autodeploy`; the venv carries `_editable_impl_nava_rebar.pth` pointing at that sibling. Re-running the same nodeids with the local `src` first on `PYTHONPATH` passes | **Measurement artifact — not a repository defect** |
| Close gate's upstream scan vs. local branch name | 1 | The fixture repo's current branch is `master` while the only remote branch is `origin/main`. `upstream_branch_refs()` returns only remote refs ending in `/<current-branch>`, so it returns `[]` even after a successful fetch, and the close precheck cannot see the referencing commit | Reproduced in a scratch repo with ambient Git config scrubbed: `git init` defaults to `master`, `origin/main` exists after fetch, `upstream_branch_refs()` returns `[]` | Real, and already ticketed |

## The 47 → 33 movement was arithmetic, not a fix

It was never a 14-test class. The prior in-scope 47 had **29 drained** — 20 git-identity, 8 semgrep, and 1 `ps`, now a counted skip — while this run **added 15 new** stale-venv structural failures. `47 − 29 + 15 = 33`. The semaphore class is separately confirmed drained: the log reports `MAKE_TEST_SEMLOCK_COUNT=0` alongside `POSIX named semaphore unavailable: 4` as counted skips, which is `0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7` working as designed.

## Where the two real classes belong

Neither is this ticket's to fix. Both already have their own bug, and both describe exactly this mechanism:

- The 17 pandoc failures are `9119-3f7b` (`frenzied-snively-llama`) — the darwin-arm64 pandoc provenance hash pins an x86_64 binary, so no working arm64 pandoc can satisfy it. The probe here is independent confirmation of that ticket from a second direction.
- The single close-gate failure is `9753-647b` (`piercing-grained-elver`) — the close gate's upstream scan misses the remote ref when the local branch name differs.

## None of the 33 belong to 8c5f

`8c5f-7727`'s population is the doctor repair identity tests, and no `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py` or `tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py` nodeid appears here. The two `identity_ts2` failures look related by name only — they are tree-scan failures from the stale editable install, and they pass with the local `src` first on `PYTHONPATH`.

## The operating correction this forces

Running a sibling worktree's venv by `PATH` prefix is sound for `git commit`, `ruff` and `rebar`, but it is **wrong for pytest**: the editable install resolves `rebar` to whichever worktree provisioned the venv, so every tree-scan test silently compares two different checkouts. Any measurement of this ticket's population taken that way inflates the count. A run intended as evidence needs a venv whose editable install points at the worktree under test, or the worktree's own `src` first on `PYTHONPATH`.

compiled_state.description:
## Status: remediation, scope narrowed after plan review

The census this ticket originally planned is complete and recorded in the comments. Plan review then established that the pandoc population does not belong here, so it has been split to `dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7`. This ticket now covers **29** failures across **3** causes.

## Established findings

`make test` under the agent sandbox on unmodified `origin/main` fails **51** tests, reproducibly, with no nondeterminism across repeated runs. The split:

| Cause | Count | Mechanism | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Git identity | 20 | The harness exports command-scope `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n`, which every inherited-environment git subprocess honors over repo-local config | **This ticket** |
| semgrep | 8 | Writing the real-home `~/.semgrep/settings.yml` is denied | **This ticket** |
| `ps` | 1 | Process enumeration denied — the only genuine sandbox denial | **This ticket** |
| pandoc | 17 | Bundled `pypandoc` binary is x86_64 on arm64 | `dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7` |
| SemLock | 4 | Darwin `sem_open` denied with `EPERM` | `0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7` |
| Close gate | 1 | Ordinary baseline defect, unrelated to environment | `9753-647b-2f85-40ef` |

**Worker count is not a remedy for any part of this.** The runner-level (pytest-xdist) failure population measured exactly **0**; xdist brings its pool up successfully and reaches 99% of the suite. `PYTEST_WORKERS=1` does not bypass xdist at all, since `make test` hardcodes `-n $(PYTEST_WORKERS)`.

**Attribution at verification time.** Each of the 29 failures is enumerated by pytest nodeid in the census comment on this ticket, grouped by cause. Verification checks those named nodeids individually rather than inferring a cause from a residual count, so a newly-introduced failure cannot be mistaken for a fixed one.

## Approach

### 1. Git identity (20) — consolidate the existing helper, do not write a second one

A scrub for exactly this already exists: `scrub_ambient_git_config()` in `tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py:26`, covering the same four prefixes (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`), called at lines 41 and 143, with a docstring naming the same harness cause.

Writing a second copy in `tests/conftest.py` would duplicate a mechanism and invite the two to drift — and a duplicated `test_helper` is itself what the mechanism-delta ratchet flags. Instead: **lift `scrub_ambient_git_config` and its `_GIT_CONFIG_INJECTION_PREFIXES` into a shared `tests/` helper module**, and have both the existing bridge call sites and the new conftest fixture import the one implementation. Net mechanism count does not increase.

Population note: 20 is the count of currently **failing** tests attributable to this cause. Removing the injected variables makes 28 identity tests pass, a superset that includes 8 which already pass and must continue to. The acceptance criteria below are stated against the failing population of 20.

### 2. semgrep (8)

Redirect the settings path to a per-run scratch location so the real home is never written. Measured: all 8 pass under a redirected `HOME`. Prefer semgrep's own settings-path variable over redirecting `HOME` wholesale, since a blanket `HOME` redirect silently changes behaviour for anything else in the process that reads it.

### 3. `ps` (1)

No remedy exists; enumeration is denied outright. This is the single test that legitimately cannot run, and it takes a counted skip.

### 4. Skip accounting under xdist — controller-side aggregation

The counted-skip signal is the property this ticket exists to enforce, and a naive session-scoped counter **does not deliver it**: under xdist each worker is a separate process, so a per-worker counter reports fragments or zero rather than a suite total, and the no-silent-skips guarantee fails exactly where it is needed.

Aggregate on the controller: workers publish their counts through the xdist `workeroutput` mechanism, and the controller sums them in `pytest_terminal_summary`. The accounting test must run **with xdist enabled**, because a test that only passes single-process would not exercise the failure mode.

### Constraints

- **Capability probes only, never environment-name heuristics.** Detection attempts the operation and observes the outcome. Username, hostname, and CI variables are not acceptable discriminators. A probe is also what keeps this portable: it behaves correctly under any CI provider and under none.
- **No CI coverage may be lost.** Probes resolve to available in CI, so the skip paths are unreachable there.
- Any genuinely new mechanism carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker at its definition site naming this ticket. The baseline is not hand-edited.

## Testing strategy

TDD throughout: each cause gets a failing test written first, then the fix.

- Probe correctness is tested against a **stub** that simulates the denied capability, not against the ambient environment, so the tests assert the same thing on a host that has the capability and one that does not.
- Each probe gets a positive-path test proving it reports "available" when the capability works, so a probe hardcoded to "unavailable" — which would silently disable tests in CI — fails the suite.
- The skip accounting is tested under xdist, asserting the controller's summary reports the suite total.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The 20 git-identity nodeids enumerated in the census comment pass under the agent sandbox. Verified by `pytest` on those nodeids exiting 0.
- [x] The 8 semgrep nodeids enumerated in the census comment pass under the agent sandbox. Verified by `pytest` on those nodeids exiting 0.
- [x] The 1 `ps` nodeid skips under the agent sandbox rather than failing. Verified by `pytest` on that nodeid exiting 0 with a reported skip.
- [x] Exactly one implementation of the git-config scrub exists in the tree. Verified by `[ "$(grep -rc 'GIT_CONFIG_INJECTION_PREFIXES' tests/ --include=*.py | grep -cv ':0$')" -eq 1 ]`.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py` imports the scrub from the shared helper rather than defining it. Verified by `grep -q '^def scrub_ambient_git_config' tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py` returning non-zero.
- [x] A test asserts each probe reports "unavailable" against a stub simulating denial. Verified by that test passing on a host where the capability works.
- [x] A test asserts each probe reports "available" when the capability works. Verified by that test failing when the probe is stubbed to return a constant "unavailable".
- [x] The skip counter reports the suite total when running under xdist with more than one worker. Verified by an accounting test run with `-n 2` asserting the summary count equals the number of skipped capabilities.
- [x] No hostname, username, or CI environment variable appears in the remedy. Verified by `! git diff origin/main -- tests/ | grep -E '^\+.*(GITHUB_|CI=|hostname|getuser)'`.
- [x] `make test` in CI collects the same test count as `origin/main`. Verified by comparing the collected count in the CI log against a baseline run.
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports 0 new unadmitted mechanisms. Verified by that command exiting 0.
- [x] AC12 -- `make test` under the agent sandbox reports ZERO in-scope failures, down from 51. The `22` here was a forecast written with the plan; the measured result beat it. Full `make verify` of 2026-09-20: `17 failed, 20304 passed, 126 skipped`, all 17 pandoc `Bad CPU type` failures, out of scope (`dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7`). In-scope failures: 0. Breakdown and CI collection comparison are in the closing comment.

## Out of scope

pandoc (`dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7`). SemLock (`0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7`). The close-gate defect (`9753-647b-2f85-40ef`). Whether `make verify` reaches exit 0 overall is contingent on those siblings landing and is not verifiable from this ticket alone.
